title: Write a press release and FAQ (working backwards)
summary: Before building, write a one-page press release announcing the finished product, plus a list of tough questions and answers. If you cannot write a convincing release, the idea is not ready yet.

beginner: Write a headline that names the product and the main benefit for the user.
In the first paragraph, say who it is for and what it lets them do.
Describe the problem it solves, in the user's words.
Explain how it solves it, without technical detail.
Add a made-up quote from a user describing the difference it makes.
Write an FAQ: the questions users would ask, then the hard internal ones about cost, risk and how it will be built.
intermediate: Write a one-page press release from the user's point of view.
Write customer and internal FAQs covering the hardest questions.
Review with the team and stakeholders, and rewrite until the benefit is clear.
Use open FAQ questions to guide the next round of testing.
experienced: Use the PR/FAQ to test whether the customer benefit is big enough to justify the investment.
Run a review where readers read silently first, then challenge the document.
Iterate several drafts; be willing to stop if the benefit stays weak.
Keep the final PR/FAQ as the reference point for scope decisions later.

canDelegateTo.task: Edit the press release so it is short, clear and free of jargon
Answer the internal FAQ questions on feasibility and cost

toolExamples.google-docs: Write the press release on page one and the FAQ after it, and ask reviewers to comment before the meeting.
toolExamples.confluence: Keep each draft as a page version so you can see how the idea sharpened.
toolExamples.claude: Ask it to read your press release as a sceptical customer and list what is unclear or unconvincing.

definitionOfDone: One-page press release written from the user's point of view
Customer and internal FAQs answer the hardest questions
Reviewed and revised at least once
pitfalls: Writing marketing copy instead of a clear user benefit
Treating the document as approval rather than a test of the idea

leaderView.good: Big bets start with a one-page press release and hard questions, so the value is clear before building.
ask: Would a customer care about this announcement?
Which tough question did we struggle to answer?
signs: The press release lists features, not customer value.

sources.title: Product management at Amazon (AWS Executive Insights)
